title: Expedition 33 How to Parry - Combat Guide
description: Master parrying in Expedition 33 with controls, timing tips, reward mechanics (+1 AP and counterattack), PC settings for consistent parries, and enemy patterns.

sections.title: Parry vs Dodge Explained
sections.content:
Expedition 33's combat system gives you two active defensive options during enemy turns: Parry and Dodge. Understanding when to use each is essential for success, especially on higher difficulties.

Parry

  • Blocks incoming damage completely when timed correctly
  • Rewards +1 AP to the parrying character
  • Triggers a Counterattack dealing damage back to the enemy
  • Tighter timing window than dodging
  • Used for single-hit attacks and predictable strikes

Dodge

  • Avoids damage entirely with correct timing
  • No AP bonus or counterattack
  • Wider timing window makes it more forgiving
  • Required for AoE attacks and multi-directional strikes that cannot be parried
  • Some attacks are dodge-only (indicated by visual cues)

When to Parry vs Dodge

Always attempt to parry single-target, direct physical attacks. The +1 AP reward snowballs into additional actions per turn. Reserve dodging for AoE attacks, sweep moves, and any attack with the unparryable indicator. On Expert difficulty, mastering parry timing is essentially mandatory for survival.

sections.title: How to Parry (Controls)
sections.content:
The parry input varies by platform but the timing principle remains identical across all versions.

Controls by Platform

PlatformParry ButtonDodge Button
PlayStation 5L1L2 + Direction
Xbox Series X|SLBLT + Direction
PC (Keyboard)Spacebar / Left ClickShift + Direction
PC (Controller)Same as consoleSame as console

Timing Window

Press the parry button just as the enemy's attack is about to connect with your character — not when the enemy begins their animation. The visual cue is the moment of impact, similar to timing a counter in fighting games.

  • Too early: Your guard drops before the hit lands — you take full damage
  • Perfect timing: Block activates at impact — triggers parry reward
  • Too late: The attack already connected — full damage taken

The parry window on Expeditioner difficulty is approximately 200-300ms. Story mode widens this significantly, while Expert mode narrows it to roughly 150ms.

sections.title: Parry Rewards (+1 AP, Counterattack)
sections.content:
Successfully parrying provides two immediate benefits that compound throughout extended battles:

+1 Action Point

Every successful parry grants the parrying character +1 AP on their next turn. In a boss fight where an enemy attacks 3-4 times per round, a skilled player can accumulate 3-4 extra AP per turn cycle. This translates directly into additional skill uses — potentially an extra Elemental Genesis or Sword Ballet every round.

Counterattack

Immediately after a successful parry, your character automatically strikes back at the attacker. Counterattack damage scales with your weapon's power stat and benefits from certain Pictos and weapon passives:

  • Augmented Counter I-III: Pictos that significantly boost counterattack damage
  • Maelle's weapons (Jarum/Lithum): Switch to Virtuose Stance on counterattack — effectively giving Maelle free Stance upgrades
  • Verso: Counterattacks build Perfection Rank, helping him reach S-Rank faster

Compound Value

The math strongly favors parrying over dodging whenever possible. A 5-turn boss fight with 3 attacks per turn means 15 parry opportunities. That's 15 extra AP (equivalent to 5+ extra skill casts) and 15 counterattacks of free damage. Players who master parrying effectively have double the combat output of those who only dodge.

sections.title: Tips for Consistent Parrying
sections.content:
Parrying consistently requires practice and some strategic preparation. Here are proven techniques from the community:

Visual Cues Over Animation

Watch for the flash of light that appears just before an attack connects, not the enemy's wind-up animation. Many enemies have variable wind-up speeds but the impact flash is always consistent.

Audio Cues

Most attacks have a distinct audio cue — a whoosh or click — just before impact. Playing with headphones and focusing on sound can improve timing more than visual tracking alone, especially for fast multi-hit attacks.

Practice on Easy Enemies

Standard enemies in early areas have predictable, slow attacks. Spend time practicing parry timing against them before attempting bosses. The Lancelier in Spring Meadows has a very telegraphed attack pattern ideal for practice.

One Attack at a Time

For multi-hit combos, treat each hit as a separate parry attempt. Don't try to rhythm-match the whole combo — focus on nailing each individual impact. Missing one parry in a 3-hit combo still nets you 2 AP and 2 counterattacks.

Don't Panic-Press

The most common mistake is pressing too early out of anticipation. Wait for the actual strike to be almost touching your character. A late parry attempt still has a chance of connecting; an early one never will.

Lower Difficulty to Learn

Switch to Story difficulty temporarily to practice parry timing with wider windows, then increase difficulty once the muscle memory is established. There's no penalty for switching.

sections.title: PC Settings (VSync 60fps)
sections.content:
PC players may experience inconsistent parry timing due to frame rate and input lag issues. Here are the recommended settings for optimal parry responsiveness:

Critical: Lock to 60fps with VSync

The parry window timing in Expedition 33 appears to be calibrated for 60fps gameplay. Running at unlocked or very high frame rates (120fps+) can cause timing inconsistencies where the visual cue and actual input window desync. Community testing confirms that VSync ON at 60fps provides the most consistent parry experience on PC.

Recommended PC Settings

SettingRecommended ValueWhy
VSyncONPrevents frame timing inconsistency
Frame Rate Limit60fpsMatches designed timing windows
Fullscreen ModeExclusive FullscreenLowest input latency
Controller InputWired connectionEliminates Bluetooth delay

Input Lag Reduction

  • Disable any overlay software (Discord, Steam overlay) during boss fights
  • Use a wired controller instead of Bluetooth to eliminate wireless input delay
  • Close background applications that might cause frame drops
  • If using keyboard, ensure no key ghosting issues with your keyboard model

Known Issues

Some players report that alt-tabbing during gameplay can desync the frame timing until the game is restarted. If parrying suddenly feels "off" after tabbing out, restart the game to reset the frame pacing.

sections.title: Enemy Attack Patterns
sections.content:
Learning enemy attack patterns is the foundation of consistent parrying. Each enemy type has characteristic tells and timing you can memorize.

Common Enemy Patterns

Enemy TypeAttack StyleParry Tip
LancelierSingle thrust, long wind-upWait for arm to fully extend forward
BrulerFire swipe, medium speedParry at the apex of the swing
SakapatateSlow overhead slamVery generous window, easy to learn on
CultistFast dual strikesTwo rapid parries needed — treat as separate
ChromaticsEnhanced versions of base attacksSame timing, higher damage on miss

Boss Pattern Recognition

Bosses typically have 3-5 different attacks in their rotation. Spend the first turn or two observing their moveset before committing to aggressive parry attempts. Many bosses telegraph their attack choice with a distinct starting animation:

  • Step forward = melee strike (parryable)
  • Raise both arms/glow = AoE or magic (dodge)
  • Quick hop/dash = multi-hit combo (multiple parries)

Unparryable Attacks

Some attacks cannot be parried regardless of timing. Watch for these indicators:

  • Red flash or warning circle on the ground
  • Enemy targets multiple party members simultaneously
  • Grab attacks (requires dodge)
  • Environmental damage effects

sections.title: Gradient Counters
sections.content:
Gradient Counters are special defensive moves unlocked later in the game that provide powerful payoffs beyond standard parries.

What Are Gradient Counters?

Gradient Counters consume Gradient Points (the purple resource used for ultimate abilities) to perform enhanced defensive responses. When triggered, they deal significantly more counterattack damage and can apply debuffs or status effects to the attacker.

When to Use Gradient Counters

  • Boss phase transitions: Many bosses become vulnerable to status effects during their power-up phases. A well-timed Gradient Counter during these windows can interrupt or weaken the transition.
  • High-damage attacks: When a boss winds up their strongest move, using a Gradient Counter both blocks it and punishes severely.
  • Breaking enemy momentum: Some enemies chain attacks in a combo. A Gradient Counter on the first hit can stagger them out of the full combo.

Character-Specific Gradient Counters

  • Gustave: Generates bonus Overcharge from Gradient Counter hits
  • Maelle: Gradient Counter can switch stance as a free action
  • Verso: Gains extra Perfection Rank on successful Gradient Counter
  • Lune: Gradient Counter generates an Elemental Stain of the enemy's element

Resource Management

Gradient Points are limited and shared among powerful offensive abilities like Sky Break and Tree of Life. Don't spam Gradient Counters on every attack — save them for boss signature moves where the enhanced response provides maximum value. Standard parries are sufficient for regular attacks.
